question.text: The Ming dynasty was established after the Red Turban rebellions that overthrew this Chinese successor dynasty to the Mongol Empire. Marco Polo's writings about China were during the time of this dynasty.
question.answerHtml: Yuan Dynasty [do not accept or prompt on "Mongol Dynasty"]
question.clue: It ended when the Red Turban Rebellion forced Togon Temur to flee its capital of Dadu in 1368.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about dynasties of China.
swap.text: This last imperial dynasty of China was overthrown by the Xinhai ["sheen-hi"] Revolution. This dynasty fought the Opium Wars with Great Britain and the Sino-Japanese wars with Japan.
swap.clue: This dynasty's "century of humiliation" resulted after it was forced to sign a sequence of "unequal treaties'" marking its defeat in the Opium Wars.

question.leadin: This event's "Down to the Countryside" Movement sent youth from cities to farms, resulting in a "lost generation." --.
question.text: Identify this movement that targeted the "four olds." The "Gang of Four" became prominent during this period that attempted to purge any remaining elements of capitalism from a certain country.
question.clue: This period saw many "big-character" posters, the first of which was created by Nie Yuanzi, and the Four Olds were attacked, leading to the loss of many artifacts and historical records.

swap.leadin: Name some Chinese leaders of the 20th Century.
swap.text: This man succeeded Sun Yat-sen as leader of the Kuomintang and fought against the Communists and the Japanese before being forced to flee to Taiwan at the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.
swap.clue: This man was kidnapped in the Xi'an Incident, which led him to agree to a united front against Japan.

question.text: Japanese leader Toyotomi Hideyoshi invaded Joseon as a stepping stone to attacking this Chinese dynasty. This dynasty was founded by the Hongwu ["hohng-woo"] Emperor after he won the Battle of Lake Poyang ["p'woh-yong"].
question.clue: This dynasty's disinterest in its navy allowed for a surge in activity among the wokou.

swap.leadin: The Palmerston Letters of 1839 instructed the Elliots to set up a blockade of the Pearl River during the first of these wars.
swap.text: Name these conflicts, the first of which started after Lin Zexu ["Lynn Zee-shu"] raided the Thirteen Factories. A British goal during these wars was to control the smuggling of an addictive drug.
swap.clue: The Self-Strengthening Movement resulted from these conflicts.

question.text: Chiang succeeded Sun Yat-Sen as leader of this Chinese political party, which has governed Taiwan for 80 years.
question.clue: One leader of this party adapted Henry George's philosophy to form his Three Principles of the People.

swap.leadin: This dynasty's Southern period began after its emperor was captured and its capital, Kaifeng, sacked by invading Jurchens.
swap.text: Name this dynasty, which followed the Tang Dynasty and was supplanted by Kublai Khan's Yuan Dynasty. This dynasty was the first to use gunpowder.
swap.clue: Bi Sheng worked under this dynasty, which switched lines of succession due to the Jingkang Incident.

question.text: Article 1 recognized the autonomy of Korea, Article 2 ceded Formosa, and Article 4 stipulated an indemnity of two hundred million Kuping taels. For 15 points-such were the terms of what 1895 treaty ending the Sino-Japanese War?
question.clue: By this treaty's terms, the victors in the war ended by it gained favored nation trading status from the losers, and some harsher terms of this agreement were ameliorated by an alliance of Russia, France, and Germany, known as the Triple Intervention.

swap.text: Admiral Makarov was killed at this eleven-month battle that took place at modern Lushun. For 15 points, Maresuke Nogi was able to win what land engagement of the Russo-Japanese War due to Admiral Togo's sea support?
swap.clue: The British spy Sidney Reilly allegedly stole defense plans to a military base in this city commanded by Oskar Stark.

question.text: The Kingdom of Kong, which is sometimes classed as one of the jihad states, was founded by the Dyula people, a caste of this profession. In medieval Eurasia, people of this occupation travelled with their goods on the Silk Road.
question.clue: Under the cohong system, members of this occupation operated out of the Thirteen Factories at Canton.

swap.text: The Nihon Shoki attributes the introduction of Chinese characters to Japan to a state in a Korean period with this name. Cao Cao's exploits are featured in a Chinese novel named for this period.
swap.answerHtml: Three Kingdoms [accept Three Kingdoms of Korea or Samhan of Korea; accept Sānguó Shídài; accept Romance of the Three Kingdoms or Sānguó Yanyì]
swap.clue: In the lead up to this period, one side lost the Battle of Red Cliffs.

question.leadin: Founded by the Sima family, it united after the Three Kingdoms period.
question.text: Identify this dynasty, whose name also refers to a short-lived Jurchen kingdom in ruled by two emperors, Taizu and Modi. It's commonly divided into Western and Eastern periods.
question.clue: Its forces expelled the ruler Yelu Dashi to the west, where he founded the Kara-Khitan Khanate with surviving forces of the Liao dynasty.

swap.leadin: They're not explorers, but Zheng He was a famous Ming dynasty example of one of these men.
swap.text: Give this general term that describes many servants of the Chinese imperial court. This type of male servant is castrated.
swap.clue: In the Ottoman court, they were divided into black and white groups, with the chief black one controlling access to the Sultan, and in Assyria they included the rab-sa-resi (rab-sha-re-shi).

question.leadin: In 1662, this leader sent the Dominican missionary Vittorio Riccio to Manila as an envoy to demand that the governor of the Philippines should pay tribute to him.
question.text: Name this Chinese pirate and Ming-dynasty loyalist who captured Fort Zeelandia from the Dutch East India Company and established the kingdom of Dongning.
question.clue: The Qing dynasty referred to this Japan-born ruler of the Kingdom of Tungning as a pirate because he was a Ming loyalist. This leader later captured Dutch Formosa in 1662.

swap.text: This Confucian scholar and Han official usurped power in 9 CE, founding the Xin Dynasty, which only saw one ruler
swap.clue: Flooding exacerbated tensions between this man's government and the peasantry, leading a faction called the Chimei ] to oppose him.

question.text: The worship of Guan Yu became widespread in China because of this Ming dynasty novel, which details the rebellion of Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, and Liu Bei agains Cao Cao.
question.answerHtml: Romance of the Three Kingdoms [or Chronicle of the Three Kingdoms; or Sānguó Yănyì; or Sānguó zhi Yănyì; or Sānguó Zhì]
question.clue: A man who later imprisons Hua Tuo is defeated at the Battle of the Red Cliffs by Zhuge Liang, while Guan Yu and Zhang Fei join Liu Bei in this work's first chapter, which sees the three of them make the Oath of the Peach Garden.

swap.text: A group of Muslim mercenaries from Bukhara were settled near this city by Emperor Shenzhong of Song, whose capital was here. This city fell to Jurchen invaders in 1127.
swap.clue: The scroll painting Along the River During the Qingming Festival likely depicts the splendor of this capital city before its final two emperors, Qinzong ("cheen-dzong") and Huizong ("hway-dzong"), were captured in the Jingkang Incident.

question.leadin: In a battle named for this location, Charles Elliot ordered British ships to fire on Chinese junks enforcing a food sale embargo that had been triggered by a deadly bar fight, thus beginning the First Opium War.
question.text: Identify this location that is often said to include a namesake peninsula. The 14K ("fourteen-K") organization enjoyed near-autonomy in a neighborhood named for this location that was demolished in the 1990s.
question.answerHtml: Kowloon [or Gáulùhng or Jǐulóng; accept Kowloon Peninsula or Kowloon Walled City]

swap.leadin: This dynasty carried on extensive border wars with the Song Dynasty, and had a two separate government systems for the nomadic tribes of the north and its Chinese subjects in the south.
swap.text: Name this dynasty of Khitans that was toppled by the Jurchen in 1125.
swap.clue: After the demise of this dynasty, Yelu Dashi fled to Central Asia and established a successor state.
